memory_update.text: Core OEM candidates for electrical_equipment_transformers_switchgear are ETN, VRT, GEV, ABB, HUBB and POWL.
Second-order balance-of-system and deployment candidates include NVT, ATKR, WCC, PWR, MTZ, ITRI, GNRC, BDC and MYRG.

For this node, the strongest chokepoint evidence to track is backlog duration, book-to-bill, pricing, utility qualification, North American capacity, data-center order mix, transformer/switchgear lead times and substation project delays.

Several major non-US electrical equipment leaders such as Schneider Electric and Siemens have high node relevance but are not clean US-listed common-stock candidates; ADR/foreign-listing treatment should be handled separately if the dashboard supports non-US listings.
Pure-play transformer manufacturers are underrepresented in large US-listed equities; some exposure may sit inside diversified OEMs, private companies, foreign-listed companies or smaller issuers.

node: Power transformers, switchgear, breakers, UPS, electrical balance-of-system
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the electrical equipment / grid balance-of-system node. The strongest direct-exposure candidates are diversified electrical OEMs, data-center power/cooling vendors, grid equipment makers, specialty switchgear manufacturers, distributors, and grid construction contractors. Second-order candidates include cable/connectivity suppliers, enclosure and conduit suppliers, metering/grid-edge software vendors, and backup-power providers. This is a research universe only, not a recommendation list.
